title: HTTP Request Reader
description: When the Pico asks the buddy server a question, it sends a short HTTP POST: a request line, four headers, a blank line, and a 73-byte JSON body, 194 bytes in all. Each part has one job, and getting a single number wrong, such as Content-Length, changes what the server does.
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: Open Study Buddy
Wi-Fi, HTTP, and Connecting to the Agent
HTTP POST
Request Line
Header
Content-Length
Status Code

learningObjectives: The learner will interpret the parts of an HTTP POST request and its reply by answering 8 questions about the request text, with at least 7 of 8 correct.
prerequisites: HTTP protocol, request line, header, blank line, body, Content-Length, status code, HTTP POST (all defined in this chapter above this block).

accessibility.notes: describe() provides a screen-reader description; all controls are native HTML elements.

userInterface.layoutPattern: drawing region above a control region

controls.name: Answer A, B, C
controls.purpose: Choose an answer. One attempt per question.

controls.name: Start over
controls.purpose: Return to question 1 with a fresh score.

controls.name: Hover over a line
controls.purpose: Read what the line is called (exploration, not scored).

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Explore, then fixed-order practice items with one attempt each and immediate explained feedback
keyQuestions: Why must the blank line be there?
Why does a too-small Content-Length fail fast while a too-large one hangs?
Whose mistake is a 4xx status, and whose a 5xx?
commonMisconceptions: (1) The blank line is optional decoration. (2) A wrong Content-Length is harmless. (3) A 4xx status means the server is broken. (4) The body can be longer than Content-Length says.
assessmentOpportunities: Answer all eight questions. Mastery is 7 of 8 correct on the first attempt.
